title: James Rodriguez joins Atletico Nacional, the 14th club of his senior career
content:
Former Real Madrid midfielder James Rodriguez has joined Colombian side Atletico Nacional, the 14th club of his career and sixth since 2023.

The Medellin-based club, the most successful in Colombia, announced the arrival of the national team captain on Friday.

James, 35, left Major League Soccer (MLS) side Minnesota United in June, after the expiration of his contract. The Athletic reported that Minnesota wanted to honour James’ wishes and would not pick up the option of extending his deal by a further six months unless he wanted them to.

The Colombia captain made just eight appearances for Minnesota, who he joined from Mexican side Club Leon in February, failing to score.

Despite a nomadic few years in his club career, James has remained a regular member of the Colombian national team and started as captain in all five of his nation’s World Cup matches this summer.

He has scored 31 goals in 131 international appearances and now joins Atletico Nacional, the reining Copa Colombia holders and the record 18-time winners of the national league.

Since the start of 2023, James has played club football with Olympiacos, Sao Paolo, Rayo Vallecano, Club Leon and Minnesota. He has struggled to make a significant impact during those spells, with his success mostly coming in Mexico with Leon, where he was captain and recorded five goals and nine assists in 34 appearances.

James made 125 appearances for Real Madrid and won the Champions League twice with the Spanish club after he joined from Monaco in 2014 following a World Cup where he finished as the tournament’s top goalscorer.
